lock.integrityResult: 11/11 dependency archives match their lock checksums; 11/11 extracted archives are identical to the registry src trees (.cargo-ok = {"v":1}). The registry src dir also holds an unrelated syn-2.0.119 (generator lock), which is not in this lock.

cfgAnyEdges.finding: The lock lists serde_json->serde and serde_core->serde_derive. Both are [target.'cfg(any())'.dependencies] entries (cargo metadata dep_kinds target = cfg(any())). cfg(any()) is false on every target. They only constrain version resolution; they are never compiled edges. They appear in cargo tree --target all but not in the host tree.

closure.buildEdges: No [build-dependencies] in any closure crate; cargo tree -e build shows only the root
closure.devDependencies: Dependency crates' dev-dependencies are not resolved or built for consumers and do not appear in the lock or resolve graph: itoa criterion; memchr quickcheck; proc-macro2 flate2/quote/rayon/rustversion/tar; quote rustversion/trybuild; serde_core serde/serde_derive; serde_derive serde; serde_json automod/indoc/ref-cast/rustversion/serde/serde_bytes/serde_derive/serde_stacker/trybuild; syn anyhow/automod/insta/ref-cast/rustversion/syn-test-suite/termcolor/flate2/rayon/reqwest/tar/walkdir; unicode-ident fst/rand/roaring/ucd-trie/unicode-xid/criterion; zmij num-bigint/num-integer/num_cpus/opt-level/rand/ryu/criterion

observedBuildScriptOutputs.source: /tmp/opensip-implementation/m1-eight-output-trial-01/compile-rust/target/debug/build/*/output (earlier build; that root's Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock sha256 equal the frozen subject-01 copies; not re-run in this audit)
observedBuildScriptOutputs.limit: Observed for a debug profile on darwin arm64 with rustc 1.95.0 only. zmij opt_level="s" and other toolchain-dependent cfgs can differ under other profiles, targets, toolchains, wrappers or RUSTFLAGS.

procMacroExecution.effects: Runs in-process inside rustc on the build host with the compiler's full privileges. Source scan found no fs, net, process or env access. Compile-time env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION_PATCH") only. std::thread::panicking() is used in the Ctxt drop check. syn thread.rs uses thread::current().id() for ThreadBound. proc-macro2 fallback.rs uses a thread_local! source map. None of these are runtime effects of the contracts crate.
procMacroExecution.sandbox: Neither proc macros nor build scripts are sandboxed by cargo or rustc. Under TCB-SCOPE-01 they are build-host trusted code.

buildTimeEffects.separationFromRuntime: All build-script and proc-macro effects happen on the build host at compile time. Their only product is cfg flags, a constant private.rs module, and the expanded derive code compiled into the carriers. None of this code is linked into the contracts runtime artifact.

generatedCarriers.imports: Only use super::{evidence,identity,invocation,output,protocol}::* and use super::evidence::error; mod.rs declares five modules; #![allow(unused_imports)]
generatedCarriers.falsePositiveTokenHits: include_suppressed/include_start/include_min/include_max identifiers, Box<Policy*Predicate>, and doc strings containing 'imported'/'produced'
generatedCarriers.result: No runtime filesystem, process, network, randomness, clock, provider, storage or UI imports or effects. serde_json reader/writer helper APIs are not referenced.

latentHelperApisNotUsedByCarriers: serde_json::from_reader / to_writer / to_writer_pretty / IoRead over caller-supplied std::io::Read/Write. The library opens no file handles; File and TcpStream appear only in doc comments (a comment-filtered scan returned no code hits).

serde_core Serialize/Deserialize impls for std::net Ip/Socket addrs (string/byte parsing only; no sockets), SystemTime (duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH) on a caller value; no now() anywhere in serde_core or serde_json), Path/PathBuf/OsStr/OsString (value conversion only; no filesystem access)
serde_core HashMap<K,V,S: BuildHasher + Default> impls. A randomized RandomState is used only if a consumer instantiates HashMap<_,_,RandomState>; generated carriers use none
dependencyRuntimeCode.actualRuntimeImportsInLinkedCrates: memchr, itoa, zmij and serde_json are #![no_std] (std pulled in only through features); serde/serde_core re-export std::net and std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH} solely for the impls above. No std::fs, std::process, std::env, std::thread or clock reads, no getrandom, and no include_bytes!/include_str! of external data in runtime crates. serde/serde_core include! only the OUT_DIR/private.rs their own build scripts generate.
dependencyRuntimeCode.randomizedHashing: Absent in the runtime closure and in the carriers. Latent only through serde_core's generic HashMap/HashSet impls. The #[derive(Hash)] on 318 generated types is inert.
dependencyRuntimeCode.mapOrdering: serde_json::Map is BTreeMap-backed with preserve_order off, so serde_json::Value object iteration and serialization order is sorted and deterministic, not insertion order

cpuFeatureDetection.memchr: On x86_64 targets built without compile-time avx2, with memchr/std active (it is, via serde_json/std), memchr calls std::is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2") at runtime on first use. That is a CPUID observation, cached through a self-replacing AtomicPtr function pointer (arch/x86_64/memchr.rs). Without std it falls back to sse2 only. On aarch64 (this host) NEON dispatch is decided at compile time via cfg(target_feature = "neon"); there is no runtime detection. wasm32 is compile-time simd128. serde_json uses memchr in SliceRead error-position computation (memrchr, memchr_iter) and string scanning (memchr2). Result values are target-invariant; only the code path differs.
cpuFeatureDetection.zmij: Code selection is compile-time cfg only (target_arch/target_feature/miri, plus the build-script opt_level cfg); no runtime detection.

dependencyRuntimeCode.potentialFileHandles: None opened by any runtime crate; only latent generic io traits
dependencyRuntimeCode.threadsOrGlobals: memchr x86_64 dispatch statics are AtomicPtr (a process-global mutable function pointer, initialized racily but idempotently). No static mut in runtime crates. No threads spawned.
dependencyRuntimeCode.resourceBehavior: serde_json limits nesting depth to 128 but enforces no input-size or allocation limits. Memory grows with input size. Bounding inputs is the caller or admission owner's responsibility, not the carriers'.

unsafeAndNativeCode.method: Token count of \bunsafe\b in src/ (includes doc/comment occurrences). This is not a soundness review.

serde_json.kinds: UTF-8 unchecked conversions (ser.rs, read.rs, value/mod.rs), unreachable_unchecked, pointer offset_from in read.rs, raw pointer writes for UTF-8 encoding in read.rs, RawValue transmutes in raw.rs (raw_value feature off; module compiled only under that feature)

itoa.kinds: MaybeUninit buffers, get_unchecked, unreachable_unchecked, ptr copies

memchr.kinds: SIMD intrinsics (sse2/avx2/neon/simd128), raw pointer scanning, #[target_feature] functions and runtime-dispatched function pointers

zmij.kinds: raw pointer table loads, SIMD intrinsics, and 5 core::arch::asm! invocations whose template is only a comment ('/*{0}*/') with inout(reg)/inout(vreg) register operands, gated on x86_64/aarch64 and not(miri) and used as codegen hints; #![deny(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]

syn.note: extern "C" matches are doc comments describing Rust syntax

unsafeAndNativeCode.ffi: No extern blocks, #[link], no_mangle, export_name or global_asm! in any of the 11 crates' src (syn hits are doc comments). No package declares links. No C/C++ compilation (no cc dependency). No native library linkage beyond std.
unsafeAndNativeCode.inlineAssembly: zmij only: 5 comment-template asm! sites (see above). This is inline machine-level code in Rust, not FFI.

findings.title: Archive integrity and source identity
findings.detail: All 11 dependency archives match the lock sha256, and extracted contents equal the registry src trees used for this review. Versions: serde/serde_core/serde_derive 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.151, itoa 1.0.18, memchr 2.8.3, zmij 1.0.23, proc-macro2 1.0.107, quote 1.0.47, syn 3.0.5, unicode-ident 1.0.24.

findings.title: Exact closure and feature selection match the plan
findings.detail: Runtime-linked: serde, serde_core, serde_json, itoa, memchr, zmij. Host compile-time only: serde_derive, proc-macro2, quote, syn, unicode-ident. serde_json features are exactly default/std, with preserve_order, arbitrary_precision, unbounded_depth, raw_value and float_roundtrip off and indexmap unresolved. memchr has std+alloc only (no libc/logging). No links, no build-dependencies, no dev-dependency leakage. Both cfg(any()) edges are non-compiled version couplings.

findings.title: Generated carriers have no runtime effect imports
findings.detail: Zero unsafe, FFI, fs/net/process/env/thread/time/random, HashMap/HashSet or float fields across 57,969 lines. Only serde traits, serde_json::Value/Map, BTreeMap and core value types. The carriers are inert under the chapter 14 pure-layer constraint, subject to PD-09's enforcement request.

findings.title: Latent effect-capable library APIs
findings.detail: serde_json io::Read/Write helpers and serde_core impls for net addrs, SystemTime, Path/OsString and generic HashMap exist in the linked libraries but are not referenced by the carriers. They open no handles and read no clock or randomness themselves. Recommend recording them in the dependency record so a later contracts change that starts using them is reviewable.

findings.title: memchr runtime CPU feature detection on x86_64
findings.detail: memchr/std is activated through serde_json/std, so x86_64 builds without compile-time avx2 perform a runtime is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2") CPUID probe with a process-global AtomicPtr dispatch cache. Outputs are invariant, but it is a runtime observation of CPU capability in a pure crate's closure. Absent on aarch64 (this host). Recommendation: accept it as builtin-context behavior under TCB-SCOPE-01 and record it in the TCB inventory. The alternative (serde_json default-features=false + alloc) removes the probe but changes the planned selection and drops std io/Error integration; it was not evaluated here.

findings.title: Unsafe Rust and comment-template inline asm in the runtime closure
findings.detail: serde_json (16 tokens), itoa (13), memchr (340; SIMD), zmij (70 + 5 comment-only asm! register hints) and serde/serde_core (2 each) contain unsafe code linked into contracts. No FFI or native linkage was found. TCB-SCOPE-01 trusts native code, but these crates' unsafe code needs explicit policy acceptance as part of the trusted native closure. This audit did not review soundness and makes no memory-safety claim.

findings.title: Build-host effects: build scripts and proc macro
findings.detail: Six build scripts. Five spawn $RUSTC --version; proc-macro2 also spawns rustc compile probes honoring RUSTC_WRAPPER/RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER/CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS and creates and removes OUT_DIR/probe. serde and serde_core write OUT_DIR/private.rs. All read env. serde_derive/syn run unsandboxed inside rustc. None use the network or a package manager, consistent with the build-plan asset rule that Cargo build scripts must not contact the network. Emitted cfgs depend on toolchain version, target, OPT_LEVEL, wrappers and RUSTFLAGS. Recommendation: accept as build-lane TCB, and have the build lane record toolchain, target, profile, RUSTC_WRAPPER/RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER and encoded RUSTFLAGS. Do not assert that these effects are absent.

findings.title: Workspace feature unification can invalidate this feature closure
findings.detail: This audit covers a standalone single-package lock. In the planned root host workspace (and the separate provider workspace per the Rust workspace policy), Cargo unifies features per target across members. Any member that enables serde_json preserve_order/arbitrary_precision/raw_value/unbounded_depth, memchr logging/libc, or serde rc/unstable would change what the contracts crate links and how it behaves (for example, Map ordering). Requires an enforced check against each authoritative workspace lock and resolved features (cargo metadata resolve), not only the contracts manifest.

findings.title: Enforcement of the pure boundary
findings.detail: Recommend mechanized gates on the production contracts crate: the dependency allowlist equals this exact closure; resolved-feature assertions per PD-08; a source scan of crates/contracts rejecting std::fs/net/process/env/thread/time, HashMap/HashSet/RandomState, extern/link and unsafe (or #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in handwritten modules); and a regeneration drift check. The selection of these gates is for the root.

findings.title: Trial consumer binaries are not pure and must not become production contracts targets
findings.detail: compile-rust/src/main.rs and src/bin/carrier_probe.rs use std::fs::read with absolute host paths and unwrap. They are test harnesses. The production crates/contracts manifest should declare only the library target (roundtrip tests belong under tests/ or a separate lane).

findings.title: Unbounded input size in serde_json
findings.detail: Depth is bounded at 128. Input size and allocation are not bounded by the library. This is not an effect, but callers or admission owners must bound input bytes before deserializing into carriers.

findings.title: Generator closure is separate
findings.detail: generator/Cargo.lock (25 packages including typify 0.8.0, typify-impl, schemars 0.8.22, regress 0.12.0, syn 2.0.119, log, semver, thiserror) is a build-time generation closure. None of its extra packages appear in the contracts lock. It was not reviewed here.

overallAssessment.summary: Based on the audit, the planned serde 1.0.229 (derive) + serde_json 1.0.151 (default) closure is substantively suitable as the pure contracts dependency set under TCB-SCOPE-01. Integrity, exact pinning and feature selection verify. There is no FFI or native linkage, and the generated carriers import no runtime effects. Suitability is conditional on root decisions PD-05 (x86_64 CPU detection), PD-06 (unsafe/asm acceptance), PD-07 (build-host effects recorded), PD-08 (workspace feature-unification enforcement), PD-09 (pure-boundary gates) and PD-10 (no harness binaries in production). Production dependency approval is not granted by this audit.
